subject: Post-call: DeltaFintech unit-econ recap & pilot asks
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@delta-fintech.com>, Adam Price <adam@delta-fintech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 17:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — DeltaFintech unit-econ & immediate asks

Elena / Adam — thanks again for the call today. Quick write-up to capture the problems we heard, the impact, and the set of levers we discussed so we’re aligned on next steps.

Summary of pain points (what you told us)
- Sporadic inference cost spikes tied to nightly settlement jobs and some batch reconciliation paths (40–60% of daily cost in short windows).
- Current average latency target is ~250ms p50 for user-facing flows; anything above 1s causes clear UX issues.
- Primary goal: move to a predictable $/transaction profile that fits within a constrained operations budget (~$75k / month target for inference).
- Secondary: keep inference logic on-premise adjacent (VPC) and ensure SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Candidate levers we discussed
- Batching: consolidate settlement requests and use continuous batching for internal flows — expect 2.5–5x token throughput savings on peak windows depending on windowing and max latency tolerance.
- KV / prefix caching: large reuse of transaction templates we saw in the call can cut token generation for repeated patterns by 30–50% in steady-state.
- Model profile: shift to a slightly smaller open model with 8-bit quantization on non-customer-facing back-office paths to reduce per-token compute.
- Dedicated pool vs hosted: dedicated reserved capacity for settlement windows to avoid burst pricing, plus a fallback to hosted variants for low-volume periods.

Immediate asks / next steps (proposed)
1) I attached our unit-econ workbook (delta_fintech_token_model.xlsx) — please fill in the average token lengths for the 3 representative flows we reviewed (user-chat, reconciliation-summary, settlement).
2) We’ll produce a short ROI snapshot (1 pager) that models three scenarios: conservative (minimal batching/0 KV cache), realistic (moderate batching + KV), and aggressive (dedicated pool + quantization).
3) For procurement: we’ll share SOC2 link and a pilot billing cap option — you mentioned procurement prefers a hard cap during proofs.
4) Proposed pilot scope: 2 weeks focused on the settlement flow (target 100k transactions/month equivalent during the test window) — goal is to validate batching and KV lift during peak windows.
5) Suggested follow-up: 30-minute config review + demo with Marissa (solutions) and Karthik (SE) on Thursday; is 10:00–11:00 PT good?

Attachments: delta_fintech_token_model.xlsx (please populate); I’ll also attach a one-page token economics snapshot after we get the token lengths.

If I missed anything or you want the pilot to focus elsewhere, flag it and I’ll update.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priom@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

---
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference platform.

From: Elena Morris <elena@delta-fintech.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Adam Price <adam@delta-fintech.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 19:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — DeltaFintech unit-econ & immediate asks

Priyom — appreciate the recap and clear asks. Quick notes:

- We’ll populate the workbook for the three flows by EOD Wednesday.
- A couple of clarifying questions for the ROI snapshot: does your 2.5–5x batching estimate assume any change to request shaping on our side, or can it work with our existing settlement payloads?
- Procurement will want a written commitment on a pilot billing cap if we move forward — can Redwood support a hard cap for the pilot period? Adam (CFO) is cc’d to weigh in on the budget guardrails.
- We also need SOC2 + encryption and key management notes before we bring this to legal. If you can point us to the docs, that’d help speed the procurement review.

Also, Thu 10:00 PT works for us for the demo.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Morris
Head of Product, DeltaFintech
elena@delta-fintech.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@delta-fintech.com>, Adam Price <adam@delta-fintech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 20:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — DeltaFintech unit-econ & immediate asks

Elena / Adam — quick answers inline and a short initial ROI sketch: 

- Batching assumptions: the 2.5–5x comes from continuous batching on the settlement flow with conservative request coalescing (no payload reshaping required). The higher end assumes you can tolerate ~150–300ms increased tail latency for queued batches during peak windows. If you can’t accept that, the throughput benefit drops toward the 2.5x end.

- Billing cap: yes, we can put a hard pilot cap in place at the account level for the test window (we’ll route billing to a temporary pilot contract). We’ll document the cap and the fallbacks in the pilot agreement.

- SOC2 + security: SOC2 Type II report and key management notes here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Q2w3E4redwood-soc2. We also have a short security FAQ I’ll share.

Initial ROI snapshot (very high level) — sample ballpark per 1M tokens ingested:
- Current (baseline): $X per 1M tokens (you supplied)
- Realistic Redwood scenario (moderate batching + KV): ~45–55% reduction in unit compute cost per 1M tokens
- Aggressive (dedicated reserved pool + quantization): ~55–65% reduction, plus improved predictability on peak windows.

I attached a one-pager (redwood_token_econ_onepager.pdf) that walks through the model assumptions; we’ll deliver a populated version once you send the token lengths.

Next steps: we’ll (1) review the completed workbook once you send it, (2) lock a pilot cap in the pilot SOW, and (3) run a short baseline vs Redwood test during the 2-week window you approve.

Marissa / Karthik — can you prepare a 20-min demo + pilot config draft for Thu 10:00 PT? Marissa, if you can include an outline of the logging/tracing we’ll provide for your ops team that shows per-route token counts and latency breakdown, that’d be great.

Thanks — Priyom

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: DeltaFintech pilot prep — pilot asks and materials (DF-2027-045)

Team — internal checklist to prep for Thu demo and the pilot SOW: 

1) Pilot config draft (Marissa) — reserved capacity sizing for settlement windows; proposed autoscale floor/ceiling; suggested batching window defaults (start with 100ms, max 300ms) and expected headroom.
2) Token-econ worksheet (Karthik) — I attached the empty workbook; after Elena sends token lengths, run the three scenarios (conservative/realistic/aggressive) and produce a 1-page ROI slide.
3) Pilot billing cap language (me) — I’ll draft a short SOW paragraph with a hard cap and fallback to hosted plan if we exceed it (legal will sign off).
4) Security bundle — include SOC2 link and a short KMS/HSM note; link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Q2w3E4redwood-soc2. Also prepare a redacted audit log sample for procurement.

Timing: demo Thu 10:00 PT, Elena to return workbook by Wed EOD, we produce ROI slide Wed night, SOW draft Thurs morning.

Marking this as high-priority for the week — want to move this to pilot commit quickly if the ROI looks solid.

Thanks — Priyom
